results.summary_before: This design plays raw unsigned 8-bit PCM audio samples from an attached SPI flash chip through DACs connected to analog pins ua[0] and ua[1]. It requires an SPI flash configured for 24-bit addressing and audio amplifiers connected to the analog outputs. The design supports play/pause control and mode selection via input pins. It is notable for integrating analog output with digital SPI flash reading.

results.summary_before: This project implements a Built-In Self-Test (BIST) mechanism for an 8-bit by 16-word internal SRAM. It uses a finite state machine to write a test pattern to all addresses and then read back and compare the values, setting a fail flag on mismatch and a done flag upon completion. The test pattern is provided on ui_in[3:0], and the start signal initiates the process. It is intended for memory integrity verification and can be tested with a Cocotb testbench.

results.summary_before: This is a ROM-less CORDIC engine that computes sine and cosine of an input angle using 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic. It interfaces via SPI to receive four 16-bit inputs and returns three 16-bit outputs. The design is tested with an SPI master, such as an RP2040, and achieves high accuracy. It is notable for avoiding ROM by generating micro-rotation angles with Taylor series approximation.

results.summary_before: This design integrates a UART and an SPI communication block into a single Tiny Tapeout tile, with pins arranged so both can operate simultaneously. A loopback input connects the input register directly to the output register, so serial output echoes serial input when loopback is asserted, which simplifies testing without external devices. The UART exposes start, valid, and ready signals, while the SPI exposes chip select, start, sclk, and separate slave receive and transmit starts. The documentation describes the top-level wrapper and submodules but gives no silicon test results or measured behavior.
